title: Water-Burial Among the Crocodiles
subtitle: Complete Single-Volume Edition · Chapter Guide
author: Gajendra Thakur
edition: First Edition 2026 · translated from original Maithili by the author himself

parts.title: PART 0 · PREHISTORY
parts.summary: A twelve-hundred-year backward bridge from philosophical disputation to Garh Narikel’s modern threshold. It establishes Budhua/Budhba, the name-saving ritual, oral and written memory, historical change and the conditions that lead to the bridge-site reckoning.

parts.title: PART 1 · CHAPTERS 0 TO 100
parts.summary: The contemporary core: Garh Narikel’s folk-cultural world meets bridge deaths, court delay, screens, privacy, money, archives, memorial politics and public testimony. The sequence repeatedly asks how a name survives when institutions reduce a person to a number or absence.

parts.title: PART 2 · CHAPTERS 101 TO 200
parts.summary: The final hundred chapters widen the scale—from a dream of a nameless planet to elements, language, body, caste, food, theatre and an extended investigation through seals, phones, warehouses and records—before returning responsibility to the village as guardian of names.

arcs.title: Philosophical foundations: illusion, self and knowledge
arcs.summary: The cycle begins in halls of disputation. Shell and silver, the enduring “I”, creation, Tattvachintamani, memory and manuscript transmission establish the epistemological questions that later return inside village life.

arcs.title: Garh Narikel and the birth of Budhba
arcs.summary: The narrative leaves the disputation hall for Garh Narikel, follows Keshava and the leatherworkers’ quarter, and turns Budhua’s water-burial, flood, accusation, time and Sonama Majhin into the origin story of the long witness.

arcs.title: The name-saving ritual takes form
arcs.summary: New-moon kabaddi becomes a ritual of memory. Invasion, literature, forgiveness, exclusion from genealogy, written memory, reason, tree, melody, wedding, epidemic and the planting of Channa Grove make the ritual intergenerational.

arcs.title: Court, migration, women’s assembly and print
arcs.summary: The elephant-crocodile tale opens onto court dates, distant travel, collective women’s testimony, the false ghost, revenge, print culture, famine, comet, fire, flood, colonial observation and the call for freedom.

arcs.title: Independence to the first computer
arcs.summary: Garh Narikel passes through independence, zamindari abolition, electrification, border anxiety, the Green Revolution, Emergency, drought, broadcast media, Gulf migration, communal harmony, liberalisation and early computing.

arcs.title: Ecology, rights and the screen-crocodile
arcs.summary: A drying channel and handheld phone lead into city markets, RTI, employment guarantees, the internet, screens, digital swindling, the market in bodies and Ujjwal’s crisis: the old crocodile acquires modern forms.

arcs.title: The next generation enters the reckoning
arcs.summary: Law, overseas shadows, Satyavrat, Gop Kumar, Chandrapal, Raghav, Aruni, Devika, Meera, Nishant, Nand and Ananya converge. Chapter -20 begins the bridge-site “reckoning of the splash” that carries the prehistory into the main narrative.

arcs.title: Investigation, return and the final witness
arcs.summary: The late prehistory follows decisions, meetings, the glass-tower web, collections, bridge work, tremor, blessings, the first splash, investigation, evidence and exposed names, ending with a generational promise and Budhba’s final secret.

arcs.title: Garh Narikel: the folk-cultural grammar
arcs.summary: Chapter 0 pauses before the plot to describe the village through soil, water, labour, women’s memory, songs, rites, craft, migration, children’s play, satire, ecological knowledge and the collective right to a name.

arcs.title: Bridge deaths, screens, court and archive
arcs.summary: The main sequence begins with Channa Grove, the right-bank village and the reckoning of deaths. Court delay, ethics, breath, screens, body markets, privacy, money, dark-web imagery and documentary evidence move toward a school, an oath, a search and the novel beginning again.

arcs.title: Rogues, dream courts and the weight of witness
arcs.summary: The narrative follows Batuknath, Chandrapal, Raghav and Lau through journeys, screens, silence and an internal court, then returns to kabaddi, mind, river, names, home, seed, letters, boats, weight, inheritance and the continuing work of testimony.

arcs.title: Stump, heritage, memorial politics and laughter
arcs.summary: Erosion leaves a stump that becomes a new centre of memory. Mapping, Gangesha’s question, memorial apps, code, festivals, heritage projects, tenders, research, rights, tribute apps, stolen names, testimony and a false ghost culminate in the laughter of Channa Grove.

arcs.title: Confession, public hearing and the child’s hand
arcs.summary: Dream court, confession, disconnection, travel, the airport crocodile, family inheritance and schools lead into women’s assembly, labour, public hearing, the constitution of names, flood, returning crocodiles, final deals and testimonies. Chapter 100 hands the future to the child.

arcs.title: Unnamed planet, elements, word and body
arcs.summary: A dream invitation tests a future without names. Returning to Earth, the sequence listens to seed, soil, water, fire, air and sky, then turns to word, meaning, voice, silence, memory, bodily rights, labour and finally the body of justice.

arcs.title: Caste, evidence and the republic of food
arcs.summary: The cage of caste and Gangesha’s liberation lead into Tattvachintamani, evidence and judgment. Grain, hunger, thirst, salt, taste, the common plate and the kitchen become a concrete vocabulary for justice.

arcs.title: Videha Theatre Festival and the road as stage
arcs.summary: An invitation becomes a script, a performance and then a question about what theatre does after applause. Procession, road, travelling chaupal and veranda turn spectatorship into public testimony.

arcs.title: Record room, seal and the consent network
arcs.summary: The investigation moves through record-room darkness, scrap, names, fear, adulteration, web maps, seals, orders, service accounts, donation debt and an iron chest. False consent, including the consent of the dead, points toward the warehouse.

arcs.title: Voice, warehouse and the invisible court
arcs.summary: A captive phone and sealed voice lead through removed papers, Chandrapal’s shadow, the Imli Ghat warehouse, city channels, Chand rooms, the invisible court, knots, registers, ceremonies, upper rooms and footprints until the city’s account opens.

arcs.title: Digital identities, open chest and the guardian of names
arcs.summary: SIMs, service centres, stolen faces and voices, the master’s room, Madhavesh, Maheshwar, blue registers, switched-off recorders and frozen accounts reveal the final network. The meaning of water-burial is re-read, names rise, the chest opens, and Garh Narikel becomes the guardian of names.

additional.title: The Book’s Final Voice
additional.summary: Seven brief statements turn the ending into continuation: drowned names return, silent stone speaks, the crocodile disappears but the child’s hand remains, truth sprouts like seed, and the story survives in every voice that says “I am here.”

additional.title: Appendix 1 · Garh Narikel Folk Lexicon
additional.summary: An extended preservation of the folk-cultural material condensed in Chapter 0: oral transmission, collective ownership, local geography, changing song forms, labour knowledge, women’s memory, rites, instruments, agriculture, water, migration, satire and the village’s moral vocabulary.

additional.title: Appendix 2 · Original Songs of the Unnamed-Planet Episode
additional.summary: The complete song archive for Chapters 101–104, retained after the main narrative condensed the unnamed-planet sequence into a dream-parable. It preserves the episode’s sky-travel, Earth-memory and name-bearing folk-song forms.

additional.title: Appendix 3 · Original Inner Tales of Nyaya Philosophy
additional.summary: A chapter-by-chapter archive of the classical examples and philosophical principles that appear only as brief undertones in the main sequence, including stories used to illuminate causation, inference, evidence, language and other Nyaya questions.

additional.title: Videha Theatre Festival · Second Draft (Incomplete)
additional.summary: After Chapter 200 the book reopens as an intentionally unfinished play. Bijji and the Stage Director face a new crocodile in wires, numbers and faceless networks; a hungry programmer disappears mid-sentence, a White Hat remains half-drawn, and the open curtain passes the next watch to the next generation.
